title: Palindrome Partitioning
description:
# Palindrome Partitioning

Given a string `s`, return every way to split `s` into one or more non-empty substrings such that every substring in the split is a palindrome.

Each partition must preserve the original left-to-right order of the characters and must cover the whole string. The judge accepts the list of partitions in any outer order, but the substrings inside one partition must remain in the order they appear in `s`.

A palindrome reads the same forward and backward, such as `"aba"` or `"aa"`. A single character is also a palindrome.

## Example 1:

**Input:** s = "aab"
**Output:** [["a","a","b"],["aa","b"]]

## Example 2:

**Input:** s = "a"
**Output:** [["a"]]

## Constraints:

* `1 <= s.length <= 16`
* `s` contains only lowercase English letters.

solutions.name: Backtracking with On-Demand Palindrome Check
solutions.description:
## Approach

Build a partition from left to right. At each `start` index, try every possible `end` index, check whether `s[start..end]` is a palindrome with two pointers, and recurse from `end + 1` only for valid pieces.

## Key Insight

A partition is just a sequence of cut positions. Backtracking enumerates those cuts, and the palindrome check decides which cuts are legal before they enter the current path.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n * 2^n), including palindrome checks and copying output paths
- Space Complexity: O(n) excluding the returned partitions

solutions.name: Palindrome Table Backtracking
solutions.description:
## Approach

Precompute a boolean table `palindrome[start][end]` for every substring, then run the same cut-enumerating backtracking. During recursion, checking whether a candidate piece is legal becomes an O(1) table lookup.

## Key Insight

Many recursive branches ask whether the same substring is a palindrome. The DP table pays O(n^2) once and removes repeated two-pointer scans from the search tree.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n^2 + n * 2^n)
- Space Complexity: O(n^2) for the table plus O(n) recursion depth

solutions.name: Iterative Stack DFS
solutions.description:
## Approach

Store search states on an explicit stack. Each state contains the next start index and the pieces chosen so far. Pushing candidate cuts in reverse order makes the traversal resemble ordinary left-to-right recursive DFS.

## Key Insight

Recursive backtracking is a stack of partially built partitions. Making that stack explicit is useful for teaching how DFS state is represented and copied.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n * 2^n)
- Space Complexity: O(n * 2^n) in the worst case because queued states store partial paths

solutions.name: Bottom-Up Suffix Partition DP
solutions.description:
## Approach

Precompute palindrome substrings, then build answers from the end of the string toward the front. `suffixPartitions[i]` stores every valid palindrome partition of `s[i..]`. For each palindrome prefix `s[start..end]`, prepend it to every partition already known for `end + 1`.

## Key Insight

Instead of exploring cuts top down, this DP defines the full answer set for every suffix. The transition mirrors the recursive choice, but the subproblem boundary is explicit: a first palindrome piece plus a valid partition of the remaining suffix.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n * 2^n), because every emitted partition still has to be built
- Space Complexity: O(n * 2^n) for all stored suffix partitions
